task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-262's marker insertion across 11 docs/issues/*.yaml files, including scope re-derivation and YAML validity.

result.note: All 8 checks independently re-run from scratch (nothing trusted from DOC-UPDATER's handoff). (1) git diff 647cab1d..HEAD --stat: exactly 11 docs/issues/*.yaml files plus this run's own step-00 and step-02 handoff jsons -- 0 deletions, 87 insertions total (23 across the 11 issue files + 64 handoff-json scaffolding). (2) Independent scope re-derivation: enumerated all 159 ISS-*.yaml files with id in [0101,0439] and grep -l '\.zig' over that full set -- result is exactly the same 11 files DOC-UPDATER touched (ISS-0101,0102,0103,0104,0105,0278,0402,0411,0424,0438,0439), confirming no in-scope file was missed and no out-of-scope file was touched. (3) Per-file grep -c '\.zig' before (git show 647cab1d:<path>) vs after (working tree): identical for all 11 files (2,2,3,2,2,5,1,1,5,8,1 -- sum 32 both before and after). (4) Per-file diff with marker lines stripped (grep -v the exact marker string) against git show 647cab1d:<path>: empty diff for all 11 files -- citation text byte-identical, confirming no path text altered/reordered/deleted. (5) ISS-0424: the '#'-prefixed marker sits on its own line (line 2) directly above 'id: ISS-0424' / above 'title:' (line 3), verified as a genuine YAML comment (not a title-field value corruption) -- python3 yaml.safe_load succeeds and 'title:' parses to its expected string; this is the correct ISS-0510-amendment technique since 'title:' is a top-level scalar key, not a folded-scalar body, so a bare unprefixed marker line there would have produced an invalid/unintended YAML node. (6) grep -rnE 'unlike R-Co|deliberately diverges|diverges from R-Co' across all 11 files, run against both 647cab1d and HEAD: exactly 1 match both times, only in ISS-0424, text 'R-Co", "deliberately diverges"). These document independent judgement' byte-identical between the two revisions (line number shifted from 60 to 63 purely due to marker lines inserted earlier in the same file -- expected and harmless). (7) git diff 647cab1d..HEAD --stat -- CLAUDE.md README.md docs/migration/README.md: empty (untouched); git diff --name-only -- docs/issues/ confirms exactly the same 11 files, no other docs/issues/*.yaml touched. (8) All 11 files individually pass python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(...))" with no exception. No discrepancies found between independently-derived results and DOC-UPDATER's claims. Idiom/scope note (informational, not a gate finding): this is pure documentation/YAML annotation work with no OTP, supervision, or type-safety surface -- REVIEWER's usual code-idiom checks (gen_statem usage, InstanceSupervisor isolation, type-safety gaps) are not applicable to this diff; no scope creep observed, insertions are exactly the marker line per citation unit per the design doc's mechanical rule, nothing more.
